answer: A stake-weighted entry queue per epoch is the sharpest Sybil defence: joining a worker set requires locking a bond for one full epoch, sized against median earnings of settled peers. Identity is cheap, capital is not, so an operator creating a plume of fresh keys must fund every bond before any earns, and payouts wait through a dispute window where peers prove collusion and claim the posted money. Attacker cost scales with fake identities and is mostly unrecoverable, so new keys no longer lower average pay. A shared vault fails: bonds must be slashable, and the zenith price equals honest cost.
